somestacks.command.help.title: Some Stacks commands
somestacks.command.help.unknown: No such ss command: %s. Try one of: %s
somestacks.command.help.gate.operator: an operator, in game or from the server console
somestacks.command.help.gate.server_admi: a server administrator, in game only
somestacks.command.help.item.summary: Set how one item is drawn inside a stack
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.1: Modes: 2d flattens the item onto the faces of its cell, 3d uses its ordinary model, block draws a block item's own block, and gui uses its inventory look.
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.2: Only the mode is required. Scale defaults to 1 and offset to zero, and 2d uses the x and y offset only.
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.3: The change applies to your own view at once but lives in memory until /ss write changed saves it.
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.4: reset drops your entry, so the item goes back to the server, built-in or measured setting it had before.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.summary: Build galleries of Storage Stacks to review item rendering
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.1: Builds east of you over a sandstone floor, nine items to a stack, rows running north. Whatever blocks stand in the floor and stack positions are replaced.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.2: It overwrites that region outright, without the protection checks a placement gesture answers to, which is why it is held a permission level above the rest of ss.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.3: <modid> is one namespace and all is every loaded one, which in a large pack is thousands of rendered block entities. list builds the namespaces of the gen mod list.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.4: items builds one row from the gen item list, sorted by mod id and then item name.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.5: all, list and items skip an entry they cannot show and report it; naming one namespace that cannot be shown fails instead.
somestacks.command.help.ingotgallery.sum: Build galleries of Bar Stacks to review bar textures and tints
somestacks.command.help.ingotgallery.det: The same generator over Bar Stacks, covering only the items a Bar Stack accepts, one bar per ingot and eight to a block.
Its namespace completions offer only the namespaces that have an ingot.
somestacks.command.help.write.summary: Write render overrides from your client to disk
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.1: changed saves what /ss item set to config/somestacks/item_overrides.json, which your client loads at startup. Only entries you set are ever written.
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.2: The namespace forms dump a complete profile for every item of those namespaces to config/somestacks/generated_overrides/<namespace>.json, measuring whatever no override layer configures.
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.3: That dump runs on your own client and holds it busy until it finishes, so name a namespace, or keep a review session's mods in the gen mod list and dump list, rather than reaching for all in a large pack.
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.4: Nothing reads generated_overrides back. A file there is ready to be corrected by hand and dropped into a resource pack or a server's server_item_overrides folder.
somestacks.command.help.reload.summary: Re-read the server override folder and re-sync players
somestacks.command.help.reload.detail.1: Reads config/somestacks/server_item_overrides/ again and pushes the current server config to every player.
somestacks.command.help.reload.detail.2: It does not re-read the world-policy JSON. Restart the server after editing that file directly.
somestacks.command.help.gen.summary: Edit the mod and item lists the render galleries build from
somestacks.command.help.gen.detail.1: The mod list feeds /ss gallery list and /ss ingotgallery list, in the order it is stored, which is the order of the gallery's columns.
somestacks.command.help.gen.detail.2: The item list feeds /ss gallery items. The row is sorted by mod id and then item name when it is built, so the stored order carries no meaning.
somestacks.command.help.gen.detail.3: An item id is checked against the registry as it is added. A mod id is taken as typed.
somestacks.command.help.deny.summary: Bar a mod's items or one item from being stored
somestacks.command.help.deny.detail.1: A disabled mod's items are refused by every stack; a disabled item is refused on the deposit gestures. Contents already stored can still be taken out.
somestacks.command.help.deny.detail.2: A mod id is taken as typed, since it may name a mod that is not installed yet. An item id is checked against the registry, because the list is matched by exact id and a typo would sit in it looking effective.
somestacks.command.help.ingot.summary: Edit which tags and items a Bar Stack accepts
somestacks.command.help.ingot.detail.1: A Bar Stack holds the items these entries resolve to, and a Singles Stack holds everything else, so widening this list narrows Singles by as much. Contents already stored can still be taken out either way.
somestacks.command.help.ingot.detail.2: A # entry names an item tag and may contain * to match a run of any characters. The default #forge:ingots* covers #forge:ingots and every forge:ingots/<metal> beneath it, which reaches a mod that tags its ingots only under the child tag.
somestacks.command.help.ingot.detail.3: Any other entry is a single item id, which accepts one hand-picked item without a data pack tag.
somestacks.command.help.ingot.detail.4: A # entry is taken as typed, since it may name a tag no data pack has declared yet; a bare item id is rejected when the registry does not know it. An edit reports how many items are accepted afterwards, and a # entry matching no tag is logged when the list is read.
somestacks.command.help.help.summary: List these commands, or explain one
somestacks.command.help.help.detail.1: Every ss subcommand has an entry, and each one names the gate it answers to: ss is an administrator's tool throughout, and the two render gallery commands sit a permission level above the rest because they overwrite the world.
